column1: # THE MEMBER AT A KEY OR A POSITION: at(d, ...k) reads what a path step
# reads, a member of a map under the key k spells and of a list at the
# index it spells, and more keys step further (task C1 of
# sketch/LANG-REFINEMENT-PLAN.0.md, rulings 1 to 4). Each expectation is
# what both engines answer. Columns: name<TAB>mode<TAB>src<TAB>expect.
# A field of each member, keys kept.

column3: svc: {a: {port: 1, cfg: {x: 1}}, b: {port: 2, cfg: {x: 2}}}\nports: pack($.svc, at(_, port))\ncfgs: pack($.svc, at(_, cfg))
xs: [{name: web}, {name: db}]\nout: each($.xs, {n: at(_, name)})
xs: [{name: web}, {name: db}]\nout: each($.xs, at(_, name))

column1: # A lookup by a field of the member.

column3: teams: {core: {email: "core@x"}, web: {email: "web@x"}}\nsvc: {a: {team: core}, b: {team: web}}\nowners: pack($.svc, at($.teams, at(_, team), email))
teams: {core: {email: "core@x", tier: 1}, web: {email: "web@x", tier: 2}}\nsvc: {a: {team: core}, b: {team: web}}\nout: pack($.svc, {owner: at($.teams, at(_, team))})
teams: {core: {email: "core@x"}}\nsvc: {a: {team: core}, b: {team: ops}}\nowners: pack($.svc, at($.teams, at(_, team), email))
teams: {core: {email: "core@x"}}\nsvc: {a: {team: core}, b: {team: ops}}\nowners: pack($.svc, {o: maybe(at($.teams, at(_, team), email))})

column1: # A condition over two fields. A bound whose argument holds `_`, as in
# filter($.xs, {a: above(at(_, b))}), reads nothing in a trial and keeps
# no member in either engine, as routes-k4 of comprehension.tsv does; a
# match over the difference is the direct spelling.

column3: xs: [{a: 3, b: 1}, {a: 1, b: 2}]\nbig: each($.xs, match(sub(at(_, a), at(_, b)), above(0), at(_, a), maybe($.none)))
xs: [{a: 3, b: 1}, {a: 1, b: 2}]\nbig: pick(filter($.xs, {a: above(at(_, b))}), a)
xs: [{a: 3, b: 3}, {a: 1, b: 2}]\nsame: filter($.xs, {a: at(_, b)})
ks: [a, b]\nys: [1, 2]\npairs: each($.ks, {k: _, y: at($.ys, key())})
ks: [a, b, c]\nys: [1, 2]\npairs: each($.ks, {k: _, y: at($.ys, key())})
ks: [a, b, c]\nys: [1, 2]\npairs: each($.ks, {k: _, y: maybe(at($.ys, key()))})

column1: # A step into a map and a list, as a path's.
# A negative position counts from the end of a list, which a path step
# does not: at(xs, -1) is the last member (ruling 4).

column3: xs: [a, b, c, d, e, f, g, h, i, j, k, l]\nout: at($.xs, -1)

column1: # More keys step further: at(d, a, b) is at(at(d, a), b).

column3: m: {a: {b: {c: 1}}}\nx: at($.m, a, b, c)\ny: at(at(at($.m, a), b), c)

column1: # Each key is read as its value, so it can be computed.
# The answer is a copy, as a reference's is: it meets what it is met
# with, and the member it was read from is unchanged.
# A marked member is read as a path reads it (ruling 3): a hide() or
# type() member is read, and its copy is unmarked; a type's copy is

column3: m: {a: type({b: integer})}\nx: at($.m, a) & {b: 1, c: 2}
